newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sees EMU boosting European competition.
newsitem.headline: Spain sees EMU boosting European competition.

text.p: The start of European economic and monetary union (EMU) will not only make the Spanish debt market more liquid and trasparent, but will also increase competition between European governments, Treasury director Jaime Caruana said on Tuesday.

"From the point of view of (domestic) Treasuries, the euro will have important effects. Firstly, the Treasury will call less on the primary market for funding," given that public deficits will be under control and debt levels will be falling," he said.
"Secondly, the market will be more transparent and, without exchange rate risk, will be more liquid. The level of competition will be higher, weighing on future Treasury decisions."
Caruana also added that decisions made by the Spanish Treasury are heavily influenced by forthcoming entry into Europe's single currency.
The launch of 18-month bills, offered at the end of April for the first time ever, are an example of this new mood.
"More than EMU, it has to do with the fact that Treasuries have to compete. And this future competition won't mean just saving more but also holding our current investors," Caruana explained.
The Spanish Treasury is almost ready to issue 2 billion 10-year ecu/euro debt, which will be fungible with domestic issues once Spain is part of EMU.
Caruana said also that from January 1999 new government issues will be in euro with a redenomination of the outstanding amount of debt.

"The redenomination is not simply dividing by the rate of exchange. It implies also few changes in the nominal value of bonds and a process which can guarantee more liquidity to some maturities," he said.
Earlier on Tuesday the Spanish Treasury announced it intended to launch a Separate Trading of Registered Interest and Principal Securities (STRIPS) market.
Caruana said the first strippable bonds could be launched as soon as July while an effective market could exist from September or October.
